sentences.text: Scutarx was a medium-sized, heavily armored reptile belonging to the herbivorous clade Aetosauria, serving as one of the earliest large herbivorous archosaurs of the Late Triassic.
This animal is distinguished from other aetosaurs by a large, triangular boss on the dorsal surface of its osteoderms — the bony plates embedded in its skin.
Unlike other aetosaurs, the frontal bone of Scutarx lacks a distinct, elevated midline ridge.

A mid-trunk vertebra of Scutarx has a centrum that is 45.78 mm long and 41.81 mm tall, with prezygapophyses inclined at approximately 45 degrees from the horizontal and a neural spine measuring 32.3 mm long, which is shorter than the centrum height. In posterior trunk vertebrae, the centra are taller than they are long.
The skeleton includes a robust sacral rib that extends laterally to touch the ilium, while the anterior and mid-trunk ribs are double-headed.

A distinctive triangular protuberance on the posteromedial corner of the osteoderms is used to identify Scutarx deltatylus, and the triangular protuberance on cervical osteoderms is shaped like a right triangle, unlike the equilateral triangles found in the trunk series.
Scutarx deltatylus lacks the "tongue-and-groove" lateral articular surfaces common in other aetosaurs.
The genus Scutarx was described by William G. Parker in 2016.

Fossils of Scutarx have been found in the Chinle Formation of Arizona and the Cooper Canyon Formation of Texas, where four partial skeletons, including the carapace and girdles, were collected between 2002 and 2009.
Scutarx deltatylus was a herbivore, consistent with most other aetosaurs.
Scutarx is classified within the family Stagonolepididae and the clade Aetosauriformes, and it belongs to the parent group Desmatosuchinae.
Phylogenetic analysis identifies Scutarx as the sister taxon to Adamanasuchus and Calyptosuchus within the clade Desmatosuchinae, and the type species of the genus Scutarx is Scutarx deltatylus.
Scutarx lived during the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
